info.name: PeerConnection
info.comment: Manages a WebRTC data connection with a remote peer.

description.p: The PeerConnection class negotiates and maintains a WebRTC transport between the local process and one remote peer. All traffic is carried by a single bundled data section over ICE, DTLS and SCTP. Application data is exchanged through WebChannel objects, which are created with CreateWebChannel or announced by the remote peer through OnWebChannel. Audio and video tracks are not supported.

Signalling is the responsibility of the client. Session descriptions and candidates must be relayed to the remote peer through an independent channel such as a WebSocket. A typical exchange is as follows:

list.li: The offering peer calls CreateOffer, passes the content of LocalDescription to SetLocalDescription, then sends the description to the remote peer.
The answering peer passes the offer to SetRemoteDescription and calls CreateAnswer. The content of LocalDescription is committed with SetLocalDescription and returned to the offering peer.
The offering peer passes the answer to SetRemoteDescription.
Each peer forwards the candidates reported by OnIceCandidate, and passes the candidates that it receives from the remote peer to AddIceCandidate.

description.p: As an alternative to forwarding candidates individually, a peer can wait for GatheringState to reach COMPLETE and then send the full LocalDescription. The connection is ready for use when State reaches CONNECTED. Changes to State and IceState are reported through Feedback.
Network activity is driven by a framework timer on the thread that created the object. That thread must process messages for negotiation to progress and for callbacks to be delivered.

By default, host candidates are advertised under random mDNS names so that local IP addresses are not disclosed, and each candidate is signalled only after its name has been registered. If multicast is unavailable, host candidates are withheld. Set the NO_MDNS flag to signal numeric host addresses instead, or configure a TURN server in IceServers to provide a relay route.

If the host's network interfaces change after the connection is established, RestartRequired is set and OnRestartRequired is called. The client recovers the connection by calling RestartIce and repeating the offer and answer exchange.

method.name: AddIceCandidate
method.comment: Adds a remote ICE candidate, or signals the end of remote candidates.

input.param: An SDP candidate attribute without the a= prefix, e.g. candidate:1 1 UDP ....

description.p: Call AddIceCandidate() for each candidate that the remote peer signals after its description has been applied with SetRemoteDescription. Only UDP candidates are used. Other well-formed candidates, such as TCP candidates, are accepted and ignored.

Candidates that use an mDNS .local host name are resolved asynchronously on the local multicast interfaces. Other DNS host names are not resolved. Each resolution is limited to three seconds and is cancelled by RestartIce or Close.
Passing an empty string or end-of-candidates indicates that the remote peer has no further candidates. Any further candidates for the current ICE generation are then rejected.

result.error: Operation successful.
The candidate is malformed, or its ufrag does not match the remote description.
The limit for pending remote candidates has been reached.
The remote description has not been set, or the end of candidates has already been signalled.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: Close
method.comment: Closes the connection and releases its network resources.

description.p: Close() terminates the connection immediately. All sockets, mDNS registrations and TURN allocations are released, open WebChannel objects are closed and State changes to CLOSED. A closed connection cannot be reopened. The object remains valid so that GetStats can still report the final counters.

result.error: Operation successful.

method.name: CreateAnswer
method.comment: Generates an SDP answer to the remote offer and starts candidate gathering.

description.p: CreateAnswer() responds to an offer that has been applied with SetRemoteDescription. The answer is written to LocalDescription and must be committed by passing it to SetLocalDescription before it is sent to the remote peer.

Candidate gathering begins when the first answer is created, so the STUN or TURN configuration in IceServers or StunServer must be set beforehand. The method returns without waiting for gathering to finish, so the initial answer will not include candidates that are gathered later, including mDNS host candidates. These are reported through OnIceCandidate as they become available. GatheringState changes to COMPLETE once every host, STUN and TURN job has finished or failed.

result.error: Operation successful.
No usable network interface is available, or the DTLS certificate could not be generated.
StunServer is not a valid address.
StunServer uses an unsupported scheme or address family.
A call to CreateObject() failed
The connection is closed, there is no remote offer, or an answer has already been created for it.

method.name: CreateOffer
method.comment: Generates an SDP offer and starts candidate gathering.

description.p: CreateOffer() begins negotiation from the offering side. The offer is written to LocalDescription and must be committed by passing it to SetLocalDescription before it is sent to the remote peer. An offer can only be created once for each connection. Use RestartIce to generate subsequent offers.

The STUN or TURN configuration in IceServers or StunServer must be set before calling this method. StunServer is used only if IceServers is empty. It accepts a stun: URI, for which the port defaults to 3478, or a host and an explicit port, e.g. 203.0.113.5:3478. A host name is resolved asynchronously.

The method returns without waiting for gathering to finish, so the initial offer will not include candidates that are gathered later, including mDNS host candidates. These are reported through OnIceCandidate as they become available. GatheringState changes to COMPLETE once every host, STUN and TURN job has finished or failed.

result.error: Operation successful.
No usable network interface is available, or the DTLS certificate could not be generated.
StunServer is not a valid address.
StunServer uses an unsupported scheme or address family.
A call to CreateObject() failed
The connection is closed, negotiation is already in progress, or an offer has already been created.

method.name: CreateWebChannel
method.comment: Creates a new WebChannel for exchanging messages with the remote peer.
method.prototype: ERR rtc::CreateWebChannel(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Label, STRVIEW Protocol, INT Ordered, INT Negotiated, INT ID, INT MaxRetransmits, INT MaxPacketLifeTime, objWebChannel ** Channel)
method.tiriPrototype: err, Channel:obj = CreateWebChannel(Label:str, Protocol:str, Ordered:num, Negotiated:num, ID:num, MaxRetransmits:num, MaxPacketLifeTime:num)

input.param: UTF-8 label for the channel, at most 65535 bytes. Can be empty.
UTF-8 name of the sub-protocol, at most 65535 bytes. Can be empty.
Set to true for ordered delivery, or false to permit out-of-order delivery.
Set to true if the channel is negotiated by the client rather than announced in-band.
The stream ID from 0 to 65534, or -1 for automatic assignment. Required if Negotiated is true.
Maximum retransmissions from 0 to 65535, or -1 for no limit. Zero sends each message once.
Maximum lifetime of a queued message from 0 to 65535 milliseconds, or -1 for no limit.
The new channel is returned here. The PeerConnection retains ownership.

description.p: CreateWebChannel() creates a WebChannel that is owned by the PeerConnection. It can be called before negotiation, in which case the channel opens once the connection is established, or on an established connection without renegotiating the session descriptions. The channel's WebChannel.OnOpen callback is called when it is ready for use. The options supplied here are copied to the channel's read-only fields.

By default the remote peer is notified of the new channel in-band and receives it through OnWebChannel. If Negotiated is true, no notification is sent and both peers must create the channel with the same ID.

When ID is -1, a stream ID is assigned automatically after the DTLS handshake, with even IDs used by the DTLS client and odd IDs by the server. An explicit ID is reserved immediately. If it later conflicts with the negotiated DTLS role or stream count, the channel reports WebChannel.OnError followed by WebChannel.OnClose.
Messages are delivered reliably unless MaxRetransmits or MaxPacketLifeTime is set. Only one of these options can be used.

Freeing the PeerConnection destroys all of its channels. Freeing a channel explicitly resets its stream and suppresses any further callbacks. Releasing a Tiri reference to a channel does not free it. A maximum of 256 channels can be open at any time, and the labels and protocols of those channels cannot exceed 256 KiB in total. New channels are also refused while more than 4094 channel events are awaiting delivery to the client.

result.error: Operation successful.
Label or Protocol is not valid UTF-8.
Operation not supported
A numeric option is outside of its permitted range.
The channel, label storage or pending channel event limit has been reached.
The connection is closed or has failed.
Function call missing argument value(s)
A boolean option is not 0 or 1, both reliability options are set, or ID is unavailable.

method.name: GetStats
method.comment: Returns a snapshot of the connection's transport statistics in JSON format.

input.param: The JSON document is returned here. In C++ it must be released with FreeResource().

description.p: GetStats() returns a UTF-8 JSON document describing the current state of the transport. The document is a copy and is not affected by subsequent activity on the connection. The method can be called at any time after initialisation, including after Close.

The document contains a version number, which is currently 1. Timestamps and durations (timestampUs, iceRttUs and the SCTP rtoUs) are expressed in microseconds of monotonic time, and sizes (cwndBytes and pathMtuBytes) are expressed in bytes. The timestamp, ICE generation and cumulative counters are encoded as decimal strings so that 64-bit values are preserved by JSON parsers. The selectedRoute, route, iceRttUs and sctp values are null when unavailable, for instance when no route has been selected or the connection is closed.

The connection counters accumulate for the lifetime of the object and are preserved across RestartIce and Close. They count every datagram accepted by the transport, including ICE checks, consent freshness, DTLS records, application data and retransmissions. Rejected input and failed sends are excluded. TURN byte counts include TURN framing and allocation maintenance, but exclude IP, TCP and TLS headers.

When a route is selected, it reports the totals for its local and remote candidate pair, and the totals for its TURN allocation if one is used. An allocation may be shared with other candidate pairs. Route identifiers are opaque and change when ICE is restarted.
Endpoint addresses are subject to the same privacy rules as signalling, so an address that would not be signalled under the current Flags is reported as null. Server credentials are never included.

result.error: Operation successful.
Resource is in use
Failed to create a new memory block
The resource has not been initialised
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: RestartIce
method.comment: Restarts ICE negotiation on an established connection and generates a new offer.

description.p: RestartIce() discards the current network routes and generates a new offer with fresh ICE credentials. It is typically called in response to OnRestartRequired. The DTLS session, certificate, SCTP association and open WebChannel objects are retained, so data channels survive the restart.

The new offer is written to LocalDescription and the exchange proceeds as for CreateOffer. The offer is committed with SetLocalDescription and sent to the remote peer, which applies it with SetRemoteDescription and returns an answer from CreateAnswer. All local candidates are gathered again, so new candidates must be forwarded from OnIceCandidate, or the exchange can be delayed until GatheringState reaches COMPLETE. State remains CONNECTING until ICE selects a new route.
The connection must be established and signalling must be stable when this method is called.

result.error: Operation successful.
New credentials could not be generated, or no usable network interface is available.
There is an error in the provided data
Operation not supported
The connection has not been established, or an offer or answer exchange is in progress.

method.name: SetLocalDescription
method.comment: Commits the offer or answer in LocalDescription.

input.param: The SDP text read from LocalDescription.

description.p: SetLocalDescription() commits the description generated by CreateOffer, CreateAnswer or RestartIce. The Description must match the content of LocalDescription exactly. Modifying the SDP before it is committed is not supported.

Committing an offer changes SignalingState to HAVE_LOCAL_OFFER. Committing an answer returns SignalingState to STABLE and starts connectivity checks once candidate gathering is complete. After the description is committed, LocalDescription is updated with each candidate as it is gathered.

result.error: Operation successful.
The remote description contains invalid ICE credentials.
No local host or relay candidate is available for connectivity checks.
The description does not match LocalDescription, is already committed, or the connection is closed.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: SetRemoteDescription
method.comment: Applies an offer or answer received from the remote peer.

input.param: The SDP text received from the remote peer.

description.p: SetRemoteDescription() applies a session description that has been received from the remote peer. If the connection has sent an offer, the description must be a compatible answer. Otherwise it must be an offer, which changes SignalingState to HAVE_REMOTE_OFFER and is followed by a call to CreateAnswer.

An offer that replaces the ICE credentials of an established connection is treated as an ICE restart initiated by the remote peer. The local network routes are gathered again and the existing DTLS session is retained. Call CreateAnswer to respond to it.
The description can include at most 128 distinct candidates. Further candidates can be supplied through AddIceCandidate.

result.error: Operation successful.
General failure
The description is malformed, is incompatible with the local offer, or has too many candidates.
Operation not supported
No local host or relay candidate is available for connectivity checks.
The connection is closed, or the description is not expected in the current SignalingState.
Function call missing argument value(s)

field.name: CertificateFingerprint
field.comment: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the local DTLS certificate.

description.p: The certificate is generated when the first offer or answer is created, and its fingerprint is advertised in the local session description. The fingerprint is formatted as 32 colon-separated pairs of upper-case hexadecimal digits. The field is empty until CreateOffer or CreateAnswer has been called.

field.name: ClientData
field.comment: A custom pointer available for userspace.

field.name: Error
field.comment: The most recent error reported by the transport.

description.p: Error records the most recent failure that was detected by the transport while it was running in the background, such as a failed TURN allocation or a timeout during network recovery. It is not cleared when the connection recovers. Errors returned by methods are not recorded here. Check this field when State changes to FAILED.

field.name: Feedback
field.comment: A callback that is notified of changes to State and IceState.

description.p: The function referenced here is called whenever State or IceState changes. The C++ prototype is Function(*PeerConnection, RTCS State, RTCICE IceState, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(PeerConnection, State, IceState).
Set this field before calling CreateOffer or CreateAnswer to observe every state change. The PeerConnection can be safely freed from within the callback.

field.name: Flags
field.comment: Optional flags that control how candidates are gathered and signalled.

field.name: GatheringState
field.comment: The state of local candidate gathering.

description.p: GatheringState changes to GATHERING when the first offer or answer is created, and to COMPLETE when every host, STUN and TURN job has finished or failed. Gathering is limited to 30 seconds. It starts again after an ICE restart.

field.name: IceServers
field.comment: A JSON array that configures the STUN and TURN servers.

description.p: IceServers defines the STUN and TURN servers that are used for candidate gathering. It can only be set prior to initialisation and cannot be read. The value is a JSON array of up to eight server objects, with a total length of no more than 16384 bytes. Each object contains a url string, and TURN servers additionally require non-empty username and credential strings. For example:
The following URL formats are supported. IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in brackets. The default port is 3478 for stun: and turn:, and 5349 for turns:.
STUN servers do not accept credentials. Unknown or duplicate keys, values of the wrong type and invalid URLs are rejected.

If IceServers is not empty, StunServer is ignored. Credentials are not included in session descriptions, candidates or statistics. Each server is contacted independently during gathering, so the failure of one server does not affect the candidates obtained from the others.

field.name: IceState
field.comment: The state of the ICE agent.

description.p: IceState tracks the progress of the ICE connectivity checks. Changes are reported through Feedback. The overall state of the connection is reported by State.

LocalDescription holds the SDP generated by the last call to CreateOffer, CreateAnswer or RestartIce. It must be passed unmodified to SetLocalDescription before it is sent to the remote peer. Once committed, the description is updated with each local candidate as it is gathered, and includes all candidates when GatheringState is COMPLETE.

field.name: OnIceCandidate
field.comment: A callback that receives each local ICE candidate as it is gathered.

description.p: The function referenced here is called for each local candidate that is gathered. The candidate is provided as an SDP candidate attribute without the a= prefix, and should be forwarded to the remote peer for use with AddIceCandidate. The C++ prototype is Function(*PeerConnection, CSTRING Candidate, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(PeerConnection, Candidate).

Candidates are reported asynchronously as gathering progresses. Host candidates are reported once their mDNS names have been registered, unless the NO_MDNS flag is set. Server-reflexive and relay candidates follow as responses are received from the servers in IceServers. Set this field before calling CreateOffer or CreateAnswer to receive every candidate. Candidates from an earlier ICE generation are discarded after RestartIce.

field.name: OnRestartRequired
field.comment: A callback that is notified when the connection requires an ICE restart.

description.p: The function referenced here is called when a change to the host's network interfaces requires the client to restart ICE. The client should respond by calling RestartIce and completing the offer and answer exchange. No offer is created automatically. The C++ prototype is Function(*PeerConnection, INT64 Generation, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(PeerConnection, Generation).

Generation identifies the local candidate generation that has been retired. RestartRequired is set before the callback is made. Multiple interface changes in quick succession are combined into a single notification, and the callback is called once per restart request. If the callback is set while a request is pending, it receives that request. The request is cancelled by Close.

If signalling is not stable when the notification is received, the client should defer RestartIce until the current exchange has completed. Resolution of simultaneous offers from both peers is the client's responsibility.

field.name: OnWebChannel
field.comment: A callback that receives channels created by the remote peer.

description.p: The function referenced here is called when the remote peer creates a WebChannel and announces it in-band. The C++ prototype is Function(*PeerConnection, *WebChannel Channel, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(PeerConnection, WebChannel).

The callback is made before any other event for the new channel, so the channel's WebChannel.OnOpen and WebChannel.OnMessage callbacks should be set here. The channel is owned by the PeerConnection. Channels created with the Negotiated option of CreateWebChannel are not announced and do not trigger this callback.

field.name: ReceiveLimit
field.comment: The largest message, in bytes, that the connection will accept from the remote peer.

description.p: ReceiveLimit is advertised to the remote peer as the maximum message size in the local session description. The default is 262144 bytes, and the value can be set from 1 to 16777216 prior to initialisation. The limit for outgoing messages is set independently by the remote peer and is reported by WebChannel.MaxMessageSize.

field.name: RemoteDescription
field.comment: The session description received from the remote peer.

description.p: RemoteDescription holds the SDP text most recently applied with SetRemoteDescription. Candidates supplied through AddIceCandidate are not added to it.

field.name: RestartRequired
field.comment: Non-zero if the connection requires an ICE restart to recover from a network change.

description.p: RestartRequired is set when a change to the host's network interfaces invalidates the connection's routes. The client is notified through OnRestartRequired, and should respond by calling RestartIce once signalling is stable. An ICE restart initiated by the remote peer also satisfies the request.

Interface changes are detected from operating system notifications where available, and by checking the interfaces every two seconds. A burst of changes is combined into a single request once the interfaces have been stable for 250 milliseconds, with a maximum delay of one second. All local routes are discarded, but the DTLS session, SCTP association, open channels and queued reliable messages are retained.
The field is cleared when a newer ICE generation selects a working route. If a new route is not established within 30 seconds of the request, State changes to FAILED.

field.name: SignalingState
field.comment: The state of the offer and answer exchange.

description.p: SignalingState is HAVE_LOCAL_OFFER after a local offer is committed and HAVE_REMOTE_OFFER after a remote offer is applied. It returns to STABLE when the exchange is complete, and changes to CLOSED when the connection is closed.

field.name: State
field.comment: The overall state of the connection.

description.p: State combines the ICE, DTLS and SCTP layers into a single value. The connection is CONNECTING while connectivity checks or the DTLS handshake are in progress, and CONNECTED once ICE has selected a route and the DTLS handshake has succeeded. DISCONNECTED indicates that the selected route has stopped responding, and FAILED indicates that the connection cannot recover. The reason for a failure is recorded in Error. Changes are reported through Feedback.

field.name: StunServer
field.comment: The address of a STUN server for discovering the public address of the host.

description.p: StunServer provides a simple alternative to IceServers when only one STUN server is required. It is ignored if IceServers is not empty. The value can be a stun: URI, for which the port defaults to 3478, or a host and an explicit port, e.g. 203.0.113.5:3478. Host names are resolved asynchronously during gathering. stuns: URIs are not supported.
The value is applied by the first call to CreateOffer or CreateAnswer, and later changes have no effect.

constants.const: Exclude IPv6 server jobs, local candidates and remote candidate pairs.
Suppress host candidates and host pairs while retaining internal gathering sockets.
Permit numeric host signalling instead of registering random mDNS names.
Use relay allocations exclusively for candidate signalling and all peer traffic.
